caption:
Flowy clothing for bigger guys — everyone says avoid it, and they’re wrong.

If you’re a bigger guy, you’ve been told oversized and flowy clothing makes you look bigger. It doesn’t. What makes you look bigger is shapeless clothing — no structure, no drape, just fabric hanging off you. That’s not oversized done right, that’s badly fitting.

The real rule is silhouette and cut, not size. Flowy pieces with intention — a wide straight-leg trouser, a boxy-but-structured shirt — skim the body instead of clinging to it. And that’s what actually flatters a bigger frame.

Think about why Homme Plissé works so well on us: it’s pleated, it flows, it’s technically oversized — and bigger guys look incredible in it. Because it’s cut with purpose.

So don’t fear volume. Fear shapeless.

Save this for the next time someone tells you to “stick to fitted.” 👇

When it comes to Filipino food, I’m definitely more of a purist. I want to taste the flavors I have tasted since I was a kid, so I’m usually reluctant to try Filipino Fusion cuisines because any deviation from I perceive to be already perfect is like blasphemy. The Gugu Room is an exception. Their cocktails, especially the Calamansi Margarita and the Ube Babe, were delicious. Here’s what we ate and my reviews:

- Nori Spam Fries: nothing exciting. Just pan fried spam cut in the shape of fries
- Skewer Platter: tender, juicy, flavorful, yum
- Nori Truffle Fries: good but nothing too special
- Beef Bone Marrow Salpicao: chef’s kiss delicious, very rich and decadent
- Soft-Shell Crab Palabok ***: my favorite dish. The palabok was traditional but the fried soft shell crab added a salty, briney, crispy addition to a very traditional dish. 
- Bagnet Kare Kare: pork belly was chewy and dry, although the sauce is good
